speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping because you wake up frightened; can you tell me exactly what happens just before or during these scary episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To help me understand this better, does she have any memory of what she was dreaming or seeing just before these episodes begin? Also, are these episodes more likely to happen when she is fully asleep, or right as she is falling asleep?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The presence of recollection of bad dreams, distress (yelling/crying), and resolution to baseline state upon waking are characteristic of nightmares, distinguishing them from sleep terrors where amnesia typically occurs.
